assessments.reasoning: JLS SE 21 §4.2.5 gives the cardinality of the primitive boolean domain and identifies its members as true and false. The explicit count establishes exhaustiveness.

challenge.method: Test null as a putative third value through a Boolean variable.
challenge.results: That variable has a reference type. Its ability to hold null supplies no third member of the primitive domain.

limitations: This concerns the primitive type and excludes reference values of the Boolean wrapper.
The provision defines primitive boolean values at the Java language level. Boolean references belong to the reference type system.
